hypothesis: Marine faunas on different continents change in step: the genus composition of a stage on one continent identifies the same (or an adjacent) stage on the other continents, and the magnitude of faunal change between consecutive stages is correlated across continents.
pass_criterion: Pre-registered. Using Paleobiology Database marine Metazoa genus lists per ICS stage (stages >= 1 Myr) for each of six PBDB continents (North America, South America, Europe, Africa, Asia, Australia), (A) for every continent-stage with >= 100 genera, find the stage whose pooled genus list from the other five continents has the highest Jaccard similarity with it; and (B) for every continent, compute the series of proportional genus loss between consecutive stages (fraction of genera in stage i absent from stage i+1, both stages >= 100 genera) and the Spearman correlation of this series between every pair of continents. The claim is SUPPORTED if in (A) the best-matching stage is the same or an adjacent stage for >= 85% of continent-stages, AND in (B) the mean pairwise Spearman correlation is > 0 with permutation p < 0.01 (independent permutation of stage order within each continent, 2000 permutations).
fail_criterion: Pre-registered. The claim is REFUTED if the same-or-adjacent matching rate in (A) is < 60%, or the mean pairwise correlation in (B) is <= 0. Other outcomes are 'mixed'. Exact-stage matching rate, matching rate within two stages, and per-continent-pair correlations are reported as supplementary numbers.
interpretation: Darwin's 'forms of life change almost simultaneously throughout the world' is operationalised by its own consequence, which he states: that formations in distant regions can be correlated by their fossils. Test (A) is that correlation exercise done with genera: a continent's fauna from one stage should pick out the same stage elsewhere in the world. Test (B) checks that the amount of change between consecutive stages co-varies across continents (synchronous turnover). 'Almost simultaneously, in a broad geological sense' is read as within one stage (typically 2-10 Myr). PBDB continents are the geographic units; marine environments only. Known limitation stated up front: PBDB stage assignments rest partly on biostratigraphic correlation, which makes some agreement across continents expected by construction; a failure of test (A) would nevertheless be possible if faunas were strongly provincial, and test (B) uses magnitudes of change that are not used in dating.
